title: Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc
central_claims: High c-Myc amplifies the existing active transcriptional program rather than primarily activating a new target-gene set in cancer cells.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc
source_manifest.finding: MYC induction raised active-gene expression, but also silent-gene expression; total RNA effects varied with serum lot. The original exclusive active-program interpretation was not fully recovered.

source_manifest.title: Selective transcriptional regulation by Myc in cellular growth control and lymphomagenesis.
source_manifest.finding: Independent genome-wide studies separate direct selective regulation from indirect global RNA changes and reject MYC as a direct global transcriptional amplifier.

source_manifest.title: Different promoter affinities account for specificity in MYC-dependent gene regulation.
source_manifest.finding: Independent quantitative modeling tests amplifier versus specifier accounts and finds promoter affinities/MYC levels explain gene-selective responses.

answers.rationale: Active-gene amplification is observed, but independent studies disagree with the claim that direct global amplification is the primary mechanism.
The replication reproduced an active-gene increase but not the asserted lack of change in silent genes; the complete mechanism remains disputed.
Independent multi-system chromatin/RNA experiments separated promoter invasion from RNA amplification and rejected direct global amplification in favor of selective gene regulation.
